headline: The boundary is the product decision.
body: iDocHive is sold for customer-controlled, on-premise, private, or air-gapped deployment. Production data and AI processing stay inside infrastructure you approve. Public AI APIs are not required.

overview.headline: Deployment overview
items: No production dependency on the public internet for air-gapped systems
No uncontrolled document or telemetry path
Customer-controlled encryption keys, identity, logging, and retention
Signed and scanned offline software updates for isolated environments

items.title: Department Pilot
items.text: Docker Compose or an equivalent limited runtime. One document collection, a named user group, measurable acceptance criteria, and a controlled path to production.

items.title: Enterprise Private
items.text: K3s, Kubernetes, or customer-approved VMs. Redundant application services, highly available PostgreSQL + pgvector, internal load balancing, identity, SIEM, backup, and disaster-recovery controls.

items.title: Sovereign Air-Gapped
items.text: No internet access in production. Internal model serving, offline installation and update packages, media scanning, local observability, and runbooks.

topology.headline: Sovereign air-gapped topology
topology.body: Offline update media enters a primary customer data center. An internal load balancer reaches application services and isolated AI inference nodes. PostgreSQL + pgvector and object storage stay on the inside. Replication crosses an internal WAN or dark fiber to the disaster-recovery site. There is no production internet egress.

sections.title: Identity and access
sections.text: Single sign-on where available, multi-factor authentication through the identity provider, role-based access, least privilege, record- or collection-level restrictions, and privileged-administrator monitoring.

sections.title: Encryption and key ownership
sections.text: Encryption in transit and at rest. Customer-controlled keys where required. Approved data residency. Controlled exports.

sections.title: Signed offline updates
sections.text: Isolated environments receive signed application, OCR, and model packages. Checksums, provenance, media-transfer approval, and rollback are part of the update lifecycle.

sections.title: Model governance
sections.text: An approved-model registry tracks versions, prompt policy, retrieval evidence, and evaluation results. Customer content is not used for training without explicit authorization.

sections.title: SIEM and audit integration
sections.text: Access, ingestion, inference, approval, export, and administrative events can stream to the customer SIEM through syslog, API, or an approved agent.

sections.title: Backup and recovery
sections.text: Backup and restore are required. Two-site disaster recovery is designed for sovereign deployments. Availability and recovery objectives are contracted per topology — not published as a blanket uptime claim.

shared.headline: Shared responsibility
shared.body: Every proposal converts this baseline into a named RACI. No commercial terms are published here.

rows.owns: Product software, configuration, solution architecture, deployment support, pipeline and workflow implementation, agreed integrations, training, support, and update packages.
Infrastructure unless contracted otherwise, identity and network access, data ownership, lawful processing, samples and subject-matter experts, role approval, security policy, and acceptance.
Local contracting where agreed, infrastructure delivery, Arabic business analysis, on-site support, and change management.
Licensed OCR, model, database, storage, security, or e-signature components and their offline update rights.

cert.headline: Certification status
cert.note: Designed to support customer compliance programs and deployment-specific control mapping. No software creates compliance by itself. Jurisdiction-specific conformity is validated for each deployment and tender.
